questions.question: Which value among sqrt[4]{7},sqrt[3]{{11}} and sqrt[{12}]{{1257}} is largest?
What is the value of (203 + 107)² - (203 - 107)²?
If 46N is divisible by 18, then what is the value of N?
questions.solution:
To be divisible by 18, 46N must be divisible by 2, 3, 6 and 9.

As per divisibility rule,

⇒ to be divisible by 2, value of N should be either 2, 4, 6, 8 or 0

⇒ to be divisible by 3, value of N can be 2, 5 or 8 as sum of the digit (4 + 6 + N) must be divisible by 3.

⇒ to be divisible by 6, value of N should be divisible by 2 and 3.

⇒ to be divisible by 9,value of N should be 8 as sum of the digit (4 + 6 + N) must be divisible by 9.

∴ 468 is divisible by 18.

questions.question: Aman and Raman together complete a piece of work in 30 days, Raman and Manan can complete the same work in 36 days and Manan and Aman can complete the same work in 45 days.All of the three working together can complete the work in how many days?
questions.solution:
Aman and Raman’s one day work = 1/30

Raman and Manan’s one day work = 1/36

Manan and Aman’s one day work = 1/45

Total work done in one day is : 2(Aman + Raman + Manan) = 1/30 + 1/36 + 1/45

(Aman + Raman + Manan) one day work = ½[(18 + 15 + 12)/540] = ½ (45/540) = 1/24

∴ Working together they can complete the work in 1/(1/24) days = 24 days

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 hours and 24 hours respectively. If the two pipes opened at 5 in the morning, then at what time the pipe A should be closed to completely fill the tank exactly at 5 in the evening?
questions.solution:
According to question,

B is opened for 12 hrs. (5.00 am - 5.00 pm).

B fills the tank in 24 hrs.

∴ In 1 hour B fills 1/24 of the tank.

∴ In 12 hrs. B fills tank = 12/24 = 1/2

Now, A fills full tank in 20 hrs.

∴ ½ tank should be filled in = 20/2 = 10 hrs.

∴ A should be closed after 10 hrs. i.e. 3 pm.

questions.question: What is the average of the cubes of the first 13 natural numbers?
questions.solution:
Average of the cubes of first n natural number = n(n + 1)²/4

∴ Average of the cube of first 13 natural numbers = [13(13 + 1)²]/4 = (13 x 196)/4 = 637

questions.question: The average of 50 results was calculated as 30 but later it was found that while calculating, 73 was taken as 33 by mistake, then what will be the correct average?
questions.solution:
Sum of result with wrong entry = 50 × 30 = 1500

Difference of wrong entry with correct value = 73 - 33 = 40

Correct sum value with right entry = 1500 + 40 = 1540

New average = 1540/50 = 30.8

questions.question: By selling a table for Rs 2700 a man gets 10% loss, and then at what price ( in Rs.) should he sell to gain 33(1/3)%?
questions.solution:
**Short trick∶**

We know 33(1/3)% = 1/3

Required price = 2700/0.9 × 4/3 = Rs. 4000

**Detailed solution∶**

Given Selling Price = 2700

Let us assume Cost Price of table is Y

We know, Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price x loss

∴ 2700 = Y - (Y × 10%) = 9Y/10

∴ Y = 3000

Cost Price = Rs. 3000

So, Selling Price to get 33(1/3)% profit = 3000 + (3000 × 33(1/3)%) = 3000 + (3000 × 100/3)/100 = Rs. 4000

questions.question: A trader sells two articles for Rs. 14784 each. If he gains 12% on one and losses 12% on other, then what is the value (in Rs.) of the loss?
questions.solution:
Let us assume Cost Price (CP) of article having loss is a.

∴ 14784 = a - a × 12% - - - - > [SP = CP - loss]

∴14784 = 88a/100

∴ a = 16800.

Let us assume CP of article having profit is b.

∴ 14784 = b + b × 12% - - - - > [from SP = CP + Profit]

∴14784 = 112a/100

∴ a = 13200

Total CP = 16800 + 13200 = 30000

Total Selling Price = 14784 &t

questions.question: If the length of a rectangle is decreased by 20% and breadth is decreased by 40%, then what will be the percentage decrease in the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth.

Let us assume length is 100 x & Breath is 100 y.

So area is = 100 x × 100 y = 10000 xy.

Length and breadth is decreased by 20% & 40% respectively.

So the new length and breadth is 80 x & 60 y respectively.

Area after change in length and breadth = 80 x × 60 y = 4800 xy.

% decrease in area = [(10000 xy - 4800 xy)/10000 xy] × 100 = (5200/10000) × 100 = 52%

questions.question: If the radius of sphere is decreased by 10%, then by what percent volume of sphere will decrease?
questions.solution:
Area of sphere = (4/3) πr³

Let us assume radius of sphere is 100 r

So Volume is = (4/3) × π × (100 r)³ = (4/3) × 1000000 πr³

Radius is decreased by 10%. So the new radius is 90 r

Volume after change in radius = (4/3) × π × (90 r)³ = (4/3) × 729000 πr³

% decrease in volume = [{(4/3)×1000000 πr³ - (4/3) × 729000 πr³}/(4/3) × 1000000 πr³] × 100 =

= [[(4/3) πr³ (1000000 - 729000)]/((4/3) πr³) 1000000] × 100

= [271000/1000000] × 100

= 271/10 = 27.1

questions.question: Pillars are standing in a line such that distance between any two consecutive pillars is same. A car travelling with uniform speed of 72 km/h takes 18 seconds to reach from 1st pole to 10th pole. What is the distance between 11th and 31st pole (in meters)?
questions.solution:
Let distance between two pillar is x

∴ Distance travelled by car is = 9x.

∵ Distance = speed × time.

∴ 9x = 72 × [18/( 60 × 60)]

∴ x = 8 × (1/200) = 1/25 km = (1/25) × 1000 = 40 m.

So distance between 11th and 31st pillar is = 20 × 40 = 800 m

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at a speed of 54 km/h and 92 km/h, their lengths are 400 m and 360 m respectively. What is the time taken (in seconds) by faster train to cross the slower train?
questions.solution:
** Calculation:**

Total distance to be covered = 400 + 360 = 760 m

= 760/1000 km.

Relative Speed = 92 - 54 km/hr = 38 km/hr

∴ Time is taken by train to cross = Distance/ Speed

= (760/1000)/38 km/hr

= 1/50 × (60 × 60) sec

**= 72 sec.**

questions.question: What is the compound interest (in Rs.) on Rs. 2400 at the rate of 20% per annum compounded yearly for 2 years?
questions.solution:
Compound Interest = P (1 + r)t - P

Where P is the principal, r is the rate of interest and t is the time period.

= 2400 (1 + 20%)² - 2400 = 2400 (1 + 20/100)² - 2400 = (2400 × 36/25) - 2400

= Rs. 1056

questions.question: An amount was lent for one year at the rate of 10% per annum compounding annually .Had the compounding been done half yearly, the interest would have increased by 80. What was the amount (in Rs.) lent?
questions.solution:
Compound Interest = P (1 + r)t - P

Where P is the principal, r is the rate of interest and t is the time period.

Let the lending amount was x.

Interest earned with annually compounding = x (1 + 10%) - x = x (1 + 10/100) - x = x (11/10) - x

Interest earned with half yearly compounding = x (1 + 10/200)² - x = x(21/20)² - x

Difference in interest earned is 80.

∴ [x (21/20)² - x] - [x(11/10) - x] = 80

x [(441/400) - 11/10] = 80

x( 441 - 440)/400 = 80

x = 80 × 400 = Rs. 3200

questions.question: In ΔPQR, a line parallel to side QR cuts the side PQ and PR at points M and N respectively and point M divide PQ in the ratio of 1 : 2. If area of ΔPQR is 360 cm², then what is the area (in cm²) of quadrilateral MNRQ?
questions.solution:
In ΔPQR, MN।। QR, and ratio of sides divided by M is 1 : 2.

∴ All angles are equal. So ΔPQR ~ ΔPMN.

By rule of triangle similarity,

Area of ΔPQR/area of ΔPMN = (PR)²/(PN)²

Let area of ΔPMN = a, PN = 1x and PR = (1 + 2)x = 3x

∴ 360/a = 9x²/x²

∴ a = 40 cm²

 Area of quadrilateral MNRQ = (Area of ΔPQR) - (area of ΔPMN) = 360 - 40 = 320cm²

questions.question: In ΔABC, ∠C = 54°, the perpendicular bisector of AB at D meets BC at E. If ∠EAC = 42°, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠ABC?

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle DEF, ∠D = 110°. If I is the in center of the triangle, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠EIF?
questions.solution:
∵ ΔDEF is an isosceles triangle.

∴ ∠D + ∠E + ∠F = 180°

∴ 110° + ∠E + ∠F = 180°

⇒ 110° + 2∠E = 180° [∵ side DE = DF, isosceles triangle]

⇒ 2∠E = 180° - 110 = 70°

⇒ ∠E = 35°

Centre ‘I’ divides angle ∠E and ∠F in equal parts.

∴ For ΔEIF,

∠IEF + ∠EIF + ∠IFE = 180°

(∠E)/2 + (∠F)/2 + ∠EIF = 180°

(2∠E)/2 + ∠EIF = 180°

∠E + ∠EIF = 180°

∴ ∠EIF = 180° - 35° =145°

questions.question: If 2cos²θ - 1 = 0 and θ is acute, then what is the value of (cot²θ - tan²θ)?
questions.solution:
2 cos²θ - 1 = 0

∴ cos²θ = ½

∴ cosθ = ±1/√2

θ is acute so θ = π/4

So, cot²θ - tan²θ = cot²π/4 - tan²π/4 = 1 - 1 = 0

questions.question: If 1/(cosθ + secθ) = ½; then what is the value of cos¹⁰⁰θ+ sec¹⁰⁰θ?
questions.solution:
1/(cosθ+ secθ) = ½

cosθ/(1 + cos²θ) = ½

cos²θ = 1

cosθ = ± 1

θ = 0° or 180°

∴ cos¹⁰⁰θ + sec¹⁰⁰θ = cos¹⁰⁰0° + sec¹⁰⁰0° = 1 + 1 = 2

Also, cos¹⁰⁰180° + sec¹⁰⁰180° = (-1)¹⁰⁰ + (-1)¹⁰⁰ = 1 + 1 = 2

So, cos¹⁰⁰θ + sec¹⁰⁰θ = 2

questions.question: The expenditure on Binding is how much percent more than the expenditure on Paper?
questions.solution:
Let total expenditure is x.

Expenditure on paper = x × 25% = x/4

Expenditure on binding = x × 33% = 33x/100

∴ % expenditure more on binding = [(33x/100 - x/4) /(x/4)] × 100

= (8x/100) × (4/x) × 100 = 32%
